newsitem.title: USA: Hilton buying full interest in four major hotels.
newsitem.headline: Hilton buying full interest in four major hotels.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp., continuing new Chief Executive Stephen Bollenbach's ambitious expansion plans, said Monday it was paying $267 million to acquire four hotels in New York and Washington that it now jointly owns with Prudential Insurance Co. of America.
Last week Hilton shareholders approved the company's $3 billion merger with gambling company Bally Entertainment Corp., making it the largest hotel and gambling concern in the United States.

In its latest expansion, Hilton said it was acquiring substantially all ownership interests in the 2,041-room New York Hilton & Towers, the 1,143-room Washington Hilton & Towers, the 543-room Capital Hilton in Washington, and 432-room Rye Town Hilton resort near New York City.

Hilton, which had owned 50 percent of each of the properties, said the deal involves interests held by Prudential's PRISA pension fund, a $1.9 billion real estate portfolio Prudential manages for 80 pension funds.
Beverly Hills-based Hilton had been managing all four properties and will continue to do so, it said. The two companies had been partners in the four properties for more than 20 years.
The hotel chain has been on an acquisition and deal-making spree since Bollenbach came on board in February.

Last month Hilton agreed to buy most of Prudential's ownership interests in the Chicago Hilton & Towers and the San Francisco Hilton & Towers, while Prudential, which is based in Newark, N.J., agreed to buy Hilton's interest in the Miami Airport Hilton.

"The acquisition of the New York and Washington hotels, along with the agreement last month to purchase the Chicago and San Francisco properties, reinforces our stated goal to acquire full-service hotels in locations where we expect to see little new competition," Matthew Hart, Hilton's executive vice president and chief financial officer, said in a statement.
"Purchasing the interests in these four magnificent properties further enhances one of the important growth strategies our company has developed."
Both deals have been approved by both companies' boards and are expected to be completed by year-end.

David Bradford, managing director of PRISA, said the sale of the four properties was part of its strategy of investing in smaller full-service hotels. It has acquired five such hotels over the past nine months.
Hilton's stock lost 25 cents to $107.375 in late morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
